newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: FORECAST - Metro '96 net seen 704 mln pesos.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Metro '96 net seen 704 mln pesos.

text.p: Diversified firm Metro Pacific Corp would post a 1996 net profit of 704 million pesos, up 37 percent from 513 million in the previous year, average numbers from a Reuters poll of five brokers showed.
The survey completed on Tuesday showed analysts expecting the firm's 1997 profits to rise further to 1.1 billion pesos.
Turnover would range from 5.180 billion pesos to 6.450 billion pesos in 1996 and 7.620 billion pesos to 8.025 billion pesos this year, the analysts said.
Metro Pacific, the Philippine flagship of Hong Kong's First Pacific Co Ltd, was seen benefiting the most from its telecommunications and real estate units.

Smart Communications Inc, a joint venture with its parent First Pacific and Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Inc, is the second biggest cellular phone provider in the country. It had a subscriber base of 275,000 as of last November.

Metro's real estate venture is Bonifacio Land Corp in which it owns a 40 percent stake. This firm in partnership with the government is developing a new business district in fort Bonifacio, formerly an army cantonment in Manila.
The stock brokers who contributed to the survey were All Asia Securities, DBP-Daiwa Securities, Philippine Asia Equity, Pryce Securities and Urbancorp Securities.
